title: Cyril Kato's blog
description: Articles on abstract strategy board games, notation systems, and open-source development.

items.title: Specs and Tests Are Two Different Things
items.summary: A test suite is only as trustworthy as the framework beneath it, and a framework is a program like any other. Why I wrote my own, what it keeps apart, and why it took twelve years to call it finished.
items.content_text: A test suite is only as trustworthy as the framework beneath it, and a framework is a program like any other. Why I wrote my own, what it keeps apart, and why it took twelve years to call it finished.

items.title: Eight Pawns
items.summary: Nothing is duller than a perfectly symmetrical game. Asymmetry from the first move is the antidote—and three traditions already supply it. The only thing they need to share is the board.

items.title: Just a Dot
items.summary: In shōgi, a single dot separates the King from the Jeweled King. A mark with no effect on the rules—yet one that has endured for centuries.

items.title: A Linguistic Fingerprint
items.summary: The Accept-Language HTTP header as a linguistic fingerprint—a trace of where you've lived, what you've studied, and what you refuse to read.

items.title: A Coordinate Format for Multi-Dimensional Boards
items.summary: CELL (Coordinate Encoding for Layered Locations): a coordinate format for multi-dimensional board games, isolating and extending the coordinate system developed by Philip Stamma in the 1730s.
items.content_text: CELL (Coordinate Encoding for Layered Locations): a coordinate format for multi-dimensional board games, isolating and extending the coordinate system developed by Philip Stamma in the 1730s.

items.title: The Gentle Threat: From Capture to Convention
items.summary: Why differences between Chess, Shogi, and Xiangqi are mostly matters of style rather than rules—from capture to convention, resignation to inevitability.

items.title: Beyond Checkmate: A Lexicon for the King's Fate
items.summary: A rule-agnostic lexicon for naming observable king states across chess traditions, with a tri-lingual mapping (Persian, Old French, English) and a pointer to the CGSN status spec.

items.title: PCN and PGN: Complementary Approaches to Game Notation
items.summary: PCN: A format-agnostic game notation supporting TOML and JSON, designed for cross-variant abstract strategy games.

items.title: Introducing FEEN: A Simple, Canonical Notation for Board Positions
items.summary: FEEN (Field Expression Encoding Notation): a minimalistic, rule-agnostic format for representing board positions in chess variants and other board games, designed for canonicity and flexibility.
